Thousands of flamingos winter on Sebkhet Sijoumi, a salt lagoon inside Tunis itself.
The lagoons of Korba on Cap Bon are a wetland reserve where flamingos feed, and where a colony has nested.
Lake Ichkeul is a winter home for ducks, geese and coots that fly in from Europe.
White storks nest on pylons, roofs and the old railway station of Sejnane, and across the Medjerda valley.
Africa’s only native deer lives in the oak forests of El Feija National Park, where it was brought back from the edge of extinction.
Wild boar are common in the cork-oak forests of the Kroumirie mountains.
In spring, birds of prey gather over El Haouaria before crossing the sea to Sicily; the town has kept its tradition of falconry.
The Kuriat Islands off Monastir are Tunisia’s main nesting beach for loggerhead sea turtles, watched over each summer since 1997.
Once extinct in the wild, this desert antelope was brought back to Bou Hedma in 1985 and now lives in several southern parks.
Around Douz, dromedaries are still raised, raced at the Festival of the Sahara, and ridden into the dunes.
The small desert fox with huge ears lives in the sands of the Grand Erg Oriental and comes out at night.
Ferries from La Goulette to Marseille, Genoa and Sicily
